card.name: Punctuation ending a long opening clause
card.fires_on: A semicolon, comma or quotation mark that closes a long introductory or subordinate clause in formal prose. The main clause ("in this case", "it means", "it will be necessary") comes next.

modes.label: Comma after long if/as clause
modes.description: A comma ends a long conditional or 'as' clause in argumentative text, just before the main clause.

modes.label: Semicolon or quote mark between clauses
modes.description: A semicolon or closing quote separates two linked statements in older literary or scientific writing.
modes.example: during the long intervals of time between them<<;>> in this case

card.writes: It promotes odd symbols and Chinese connectives and suppresses ellipses and filler words, so there is no clear effect on the next word.
card.plain: It marks the pause at the end of a long lead-in clause, where the main point of the sentence is about to begin.
